about: The 48 symptoms of thread_finder_symptoms_backlog.md. Generated by make_catalog.py; edit that file, not this one.

event_groups.base: sched_*, timer/IRQ, x86 IRQ vectors, all syscalls, statedump (always recorded)
event_groups.mem: kmem_* and page-fault events (no probe for them on this machine's kernel)

symptoms.name: One-off delay or missed deadline
symptoms.criterion: a single iteration (or a few in one stretch) of an otherwise regular activity takes at least 5x its usual time

symptoms.name: Jitter
symptoms.criterion: a periodic activity's lateness or duration varies continuously, by a quarter of its period or more, throughout the run

symptoms.name: Many slow outliers (tail latency)
symptoms.criterion: a small share (about 1-5%) of requests or iterations are many times slower than the median, spread over the whole run

symptoms.name: Gradual slowdown
symptoms.criterion: iterations get steadily slower from the start of the run to the end, to at least twice their initial length

symptoms.name: Sudden change
asked: it was fine, then got slow around 40 s
symptoms.criterion: iterations are fast up to one point in the run and at least twice as slow from then on (a step)

symptoms.name: Slow start-up
asked: it takes long to start doing work
symptoms.criterion: the program takes seconds from its start to its first unit of work

symptoms.name: Slow shutdown
symptoms.criterion: the program takes seconds from its last unit of work to its exit

symptoms.name: Long blocked waits
symptoms.criterion: a thread that has work to do is blocked for a quarter or more of its time, or for seconds at a time (not counting idle waits for new work or its own timed sleeps)

symptoms.name: Slowest thread or bottleneck
symptoms.criterion: one thread (or one stage) holds up the whole program, which would run at least 25% faster without its delay

symptoms.name: Hang or freeze
symptoms.criterion: the program stops making progress for good: its threads stay blocked until the end of the trace

symptoms.name: Deadlock
asked: two things are waiting on each other
symptoms.criterion: two or more threads each hold a lock the other needs, and stay blocked for good

symptoms.name: Lock contention
symptoms.criterion: threads block on the same lock many times per second because another thread holds it

symptoms.name: Lock holder sleeping or doing I/O while holding it
asked: something holds the lock too long
symptoms.criterion: a lock is held across a sleep, I/O or a preemption, and other threads wait on it meanwhile

symptoms.name: Convoy or serialization
asked: the threads run one after another instead of in parallel
symptoms.criterion: threads that could run in parallel run one at a time because of a shared lock

symptoms.name: Priority inversion
asked: the high-priority task waits on a low-priority one
symptoms.criterion: a high-priority thread waits on a lock held by a lower-priority thread, which is itself kept off the CPU by a medium-priority thread

symptoms.name: Waiting on another process
asked: it's waiting on the database or the other service
symptoms.criterion: threads spend a quarter or more of their time blocked waiting for replies from another process

symptoms.name: Waiting on network
asked: it's slow talking to the server
symptoms.criterion: a thread spends a quarter or more of its time blocked on network communication with another machine

symptoms.name: Waiting on disk
symptoms.criterion: a thread spends a quarter or more of its time blocked on storage I/O (writes, syncs, reads)

symptoms.name: Oversleeping
symptoms.criterion: most sleeps end 1 ms or more later than requested while the CPU is free (late timer expiry, not CPU contention)

symptoms.name: CPU hog or busiest thread
symptoms.criterion: one thread keeps a CPU close to 100% busy for most of the run

symptoms.name: Slow to get scheduled
asked: it's ready but has to wait for the CPU
symptoms.criterion: a runnable thread is kept waiting to run for 1 ms or more at least 50 times in the trace, or for 10 ms or more at least once

symptoms.name: Busy-waiting or spinning
asked: high CPU but nothing gets done
symptoms.criterion: a thread uses a full CPU while waiting for something, making no progress

symptoms.name: CPU starvation
asked: it's ready but never gets to run
symptoms.criterion: a runnable thread gets (almost) no CPU time for a long stretch (seconds)

symptoms.name: Noisy neighbour
asked: another program is slowing mine down
symptoms.criterion: another process competes for the program's CPUs and slows its work down by 25% or more

symptoms.name: Load imbalance
asked: one worker does all the work
symptoms.criterion: work is unevenly divided: some threads of a group get at least twice as much of it as others

symptoms.name: Straggler at a barrier
asked: everyone waits for one slow thread
symptoms.criterion: threads that meet at a barrier keep waiting for the same late thread

symptoms.name: Oversubscription
asked: too many threads for the cores
symptoms.criterion: at least twice as many runnable threads as CPUs, so threads queue for the CPU

symptoms.name: Excessive migrations
symptoms.criterion: threads move between CPUs very often (hundreds of times per second)

symptoms.name: Interrupt storm
symptoms.criterion: interrupt handling (hardware interrupt handlers) takes a large share of one CPU, 10% or more for seconds at a time, where a CPU normally spends about 1% in them

symptoms.name: Real-time thread preempted
symptoms.criterion: a real-time (SCHED_FIFO/RR) thread is repeatedly preempted by a higher-priority one

symptoms.name: Slow system calls or I/O
symptoms.criterion: a thread spends 10% or more of its time waiting inside system calls (not counting sleeps or waits for events), some of which take milliseconds

symptoms.name: Too many small calls
asked: it makes thousands of tiny reads
symptoms.criterion: the program makes tens of thousands of tiny system calls per second where a few large ones would do

symptoms.name: Polling with no work
symptoms.criterion: a thread repeatedly checks for work or data (poll, select, read with no wait) that is never there

symptoms.name: Failing calls in a retry loop
symptoms.criterion: the same system call fails over and over (an error return each time)

symptoms.name: File churn
asked: it opens and closes files constantly
symptoms.criterion: files are created, opened, closed or deleted at a high rate (hundreds per second)

symptoms.name: Memory pressure or page faults
symptoms.criterion: the program spends a quarter or more of its time in page faults or memory reclaim

symptoms.name: Allocation churn
asked: it keeps allocating and freeing memory
symptoms.criterion: memory is mapped and unmapped (mmap/munmap, brk) hundreds of times per second or more

symptoms.name: Crash or abnormal exit
symptoms.criterion: a process of the program dies from a signal (segfault, abort, kill) rather than exiting

symptoms.name: Fork or exec storm
asked: it spawns tons of short processes
symptoms.criterion: the program starts short-lived processes at a high rate (tens per second or more)

symptoms.name: Thread churn
symptoms.criterion: the program creates and ends threads at a high rate (tens per second or more)

symptoms.name: Never exits
symptoms.criterion: the program has finished its work but its process stays alive until the end of the trace

symptoms.name: Slowest pipeline stage
symptoms.criterion: one stage of a pipeline is too slow for its input, and the stages around it wait for it

symptoms.name: Producer and consumer out of step
asked: the queue keeps filling or emptying
symptoms.criterion: a queue between two threads keeps swinging between full and empty

symptoms.name: Thundering herd
asked: many threads wake up but only one does anything
symptoms.criterion: each event wakes many waiting threads, and all but one go straight back to sleep

symptoms.name: Idle workers
asked: the workers are idle while one works
symptoms.criterion: most workers of a pool stay idle while one or a few do all the work

symptoms.name: Unexpected activity
asked: why is it touching that file?
symptoms.criterion: the program does something unrelated to its job (here: reads files that have nothing to do with it)

symptoms.name: Idle thread
symptoms.criterion: a thread exists for the whole run but never does any work

symptoms.name: Thread differences
asked: why does worker-2 behave differently from the others?
symptoms.criterion: one thread of a group of similar threads behaves differently in a way the rest do not share (e.g. at least twice their CPU time, blocking, or system calls of a kind they make none of)
